## 1601 N Milwaukee Ave — Zoning & Development Analysis
**PIN: 14313320180000 | West Town (Community Area 24)**

---

### 1. Zoning District

This parcel is zoned **B3-2** (Community Shopping District, Density-2), per the City's official GIS zoning layer (Ordinance No. 17230). Verify at the [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning).

---

### 2. Ground-Floor Retail + Apartments Above

**Yes — this is permitted by right.** Under [1], the B3 district accommodates a broad range of retail and service uses. Under [2], dwelling units located *above the ground floor* are permitted by right (P) in B3 districts. Ground-floor retail is the B3 baseline use. So a standard mixed-use building with retail below and residential above is a by-right combination in B3-2. **Confidence: high.**

---

### 3. Key Bulk & Density Standards

The retrieved code text does not include the full B3-2 bulk table (FAR cap, height limit, minimum lot area per unit, and setbacks for the dash-2 density tier), so I can only cite what is in the retrieved sections:

- **FAR — general standard:** All B and C district development is subject to maximum FAR standards per [3]. The specific numeric FAR cap for B3-2 is not in the retrieved text; the Chicago Zoning Ordinance table at [3] (§ 17-3-0403-A) governs — verify via the Zoning Map or [Chicago Zoning Ordinance § 17-3-0403](https://www.chicago.gov/city/en/depts/dcd/supp_info/chicago_zoning_ordinance.html).
- **FAR bonus (transit-served):** A FAR increase is available *only* in **B-3 and C-3 districts** (i.e., dash-3 districts such as B3-3), not in B3-2, and only via a Type 1 Map Amendment, Planned Development, or ARO entitlement [3]. This parcel at B3-2 does **not** qualify for the by-right FAR bonus.
- **Height, setbacks, lot area per unit:** The specific numeric limits for B3-2 are not in the retrieved Municipal Code sections. These are in the B/C district bulk table at § 17-3-0408 and § 17-3-0410 of the Zoning Ordinance — consult those sections directly or contact the Chicago Department of Planning and Development (DPD).

**Confidence on FAR bonus: high (no bonus at B3-2). Confidence on specific numeric limits: could not determine from retrieved text.**

---

### 4. Overlays & Special Designations

This parcel carries a significant stack of overlays:

- 🏛 **Individual Landmark Building** — This property is flagged as an **individual Chicago landmark** (the building is identified in city survey records as the *Noel State Bank*, rated "orange" in the Chicago Historic Resources Survey). Exterior alterations and demolition require review by the **Commission on Chicago Landmarks**. This is a major constraint.
- 🏘 **Milwaukee Avenue Historic District** — The parcel is within a locally designated historic district. Commission on Chicago Landmarks review applies to exterior work [regulatory data].
- 📜 **Wicker Park Historic District (National Register)** — Listed on the National Register of Historic Places. Federal tax credit programs (Historic Tax Credits) may be available for qualifying rehabilitation, but National Register listing alone does not restrict local alterations — the local landmark designation is the binding constraint.
- 🚇 **Transit-Oriented Development (CTA)** — The parcel is in a CTA TOD overlay (0.07 miles from Damen Blue Line station — essentially next door).
- 🏠 **ADU Eligible Area** — Accessory Dwelling Units (coach houses, conversion units) are permitted under the city's ADU program. Per [5], coach houses in B or C districts may only be established in the rear 30 feet of lot depth and may not exceed 22 feet in height.
- 💰 **Affordable Requirements Ordinance (ARO) Zone** — Any residential development triggering an ARO entitlement is subject to affordable unit requirements. The West Town community area has 20 ARO projects totaling 291 affordable units on record.
- 🛍 **Wicker Park Special Service Area (SSA)** — The parcel is within the Wicker Park SSA, which levies a supplemental property tax for neighborhood services (note City of Chicago Special Service Area 33 appears in the tax breakdown at $2,362.99/year).
- ✅ **No Planned Development** — The parcel is not currently in a Planned Development.
- ✅ **No Lakefront Protection, PMD, or Special District** — None apply.
- 🌊 **Flood Zone X** — FEMA Zone X (Area of Minimal Flood Hazard). Not a Special Flood Hazard Area; flood insurance is not federally required.
- ⚠️ **Nearby Brownfield** — Park 512 Avenue Park (EPA ID: 110005863100) is in the vicinity. Environmental due diligence is advisable before any ground disturbance.

---

### 5. Parking Requirement & Transit Reduction

Because the parcel is within 2,640 feet of a CTA rail station (Damen Blue Line, ~0.07 miles away), it qualifies for transit-served parking relief under §17-10-0102-B. Per the TOD data: **the minimum parking requirement can be reduced by up to 100%** — meaning parking could potentially be eliminated entirely for this project by right, without a special entitlement [3]. This is a significant development benefit.

**No FAR or density bonus applies at B3-2** — those bonuses are restricted to dash-3 districts (e.g., B3-3) and require a Type 1 Map Amendment, Planned Development, or ARO entitlement [3].

Verify parking ratios at § 17-10-0207 and the transit reduction at § 17-10-0102-B.

---

### 6. Demolition & New Mixed-Use Building — Approvals & Restrictions

**This is the most complex aspect, and the landmark designation is the decisive constraint.**

- **Landmark Building — Demolition likely prohibited or severely restricted.** Because this property is flagged as an **individual Chicago landmark** (Noel State Bank), the Commission on Chicago Landmarks must review and approve any demolition or significant exterior alteration. Demolition of a landmark building is extremely rare and faces a high bar. This effectively means a teardown-and-rebuild scenario is likely not approvable without extraordinary justification.
- **Historic District overlay** reinforces this — both the Milwaukee Avenue District and National Register listing (Wicker Park Historic District) will be factors in any Landmarks Commission review.
- **Wrecking/Demolition permits:** 57 demolition permits have been issued in West Town over the study period [data:permits], but those are area-wide and do not imply this parcel is clearable — the landmark status here is parcel-specific and controlling.
- **New construction (if approved):** Would need to conform to B3-2 bulk standards (FAR, height, setbacks — see §§ 17-3-0403, 17-3-0408). ARO affordable unit requirements would apply if the development triggers an entitlement. Parking could be reduced up to 100% given transit proximity (§ 17-10-0102-B).
- **Rehabilitation alternative:** A rehabilitation and adaptive reuse approach — preserving the landmark exterior while renovating interior and adding permitted uses — is far more likely to receive approval and could qualify for Federal and Illinois Historic Tax Credits given National Register listing.
- **Permit activity in the area** has been robust: 1,257 total permits in West Town totaling ~$1.04 billion in estimated construction cost, including 84 new construction and 250 renovation/alteration permits [data:permits]. Renovation/alteration permits surged 56% month-over-month in September.
